terms.name: Accessibility annotation
terms.definition: Notes attached to a design file that spell out the things a mockup cannot show: heading levels, focus order, names, roles, live regions, and alt text.

terms.name: Affordance
terms.definition: What an element makes possible for the person using it, such as a surface that can be pushed, dragged, or scrolled.

terms.name: Applied filters
terms.definition: A row of removable tokens above the results showing every filter currently in force, with a control to clear them all at once.

terms.name: Autosave
terms.definition: Persisting the reader's work continuously without a save action, usually with a quiet status line reporting when the last save happened.

terms.name: Bounce
terms.definition: Motion that arrives, rebounds, and arrives again in decreasing amounts, reading as an object landing on a surface.

terms.name: Calendar
terms.definition: A month grid of dates that can be read, navigated and selected from, whether standing alone or living inside a date field.

terms.name: Chart
terms.definition: A drawing of data in which position, length, angle or colour carries the numbers, chosen so the comparison a reader needs is the easiest one to see.

terms.name: Cluster
terms.definition: A layout primitive that lays items of differing widths out like words in a paragraph, wrapping to new lines with even gaps in both directions.

terms.name: Color stop
terms.definition: A colour pinned at a position along a gradient, with an optional hint between two stops that moves the halfway point of the transition off centre.

terms.name: Compositor-only animation
terms.definition: An animation limited to properties the compositor can handle alone, usually transform and opacity, so it keeps running even when the main thread is busy.

terms.name: Context menu
terms.definition: A menu of actions for one specific object, opened on that object by right click, long press, or the context menu key.

terms.name: Cursor pagination
terms.definition: Paging that moves by a pointer into the result set rather than a page number, so newly inserted rows never shift what the next page contains.

terms.name: Delay
terms.definition: The wait between an animation being triggered and starting to move, the unit a stagger is built from and the difference between twitchy and considered.

terms.name: Display cutout
terms.definition: The camera housing that intrudes into the screen rectangle, which a layout has to route content around rather than under.

terms.name: Dragging alternative
terms.definition: A second, non-dragging route to anything a drag can do, such as arrow keys or a move-to menu on a sortable list.

terms.name: Edge to edge
terms.definition: Drawing an app behind the system bars so content reaches the physical screen edges, with insets applied only to what must stay tappable.

terms.name: Escape gesture
terms.definition: The screen reader equivalent of the Escape key, a two finger scrub that dismisses a sheet or steps back a level.

terms.name: Faux bold
terms.definition: A bold or italic the browser fakes by smearing or shearing the regular weight, because the real style was never loaded.

terms.name: Flash of inaccurate color theme
terms.definition: The moment a page paints in the wrong theme before the stored preference is applied, showing a light flash to a reader who chose dark.

terms.name: Focus not obscured
terms.definition: The requirement that a focused control is not completely hidden by sticky headers, footers, cookie bars, or chat widgets when it receives focus.

terms.name: Forced continuity
terms.definition: Turning a free trial into a paid subscription automatically, with the card taken up front and no reminder before the first real charge.

terms.name: Global navigation
terms.definition: The links to the top tier of a site's structure, present on every page and unchanged wherever the reader currently is.

terms.name: Half-leading
terms.definition: The empty space a browser splits evenly above and below a line of text when line height exceeds the font's own height, which is why text boxes never sit flush.

terms.name: Hinting
terms.definition: Instructions inside a font that nudge its outlines onto the pixel grid at small sizes so stems stay crisp and even.

terms.name: Hyphenation
terms.definition: Breaking a word across two lines at a syllable boundary so lines fill more evenly, marked with a hyphen at the break.

terms.name: Inline edit
terms.definition: Text that reads as plain content until you click it, at which point it becomes an input in the same place with save and cancel.

terms.name: Italic
terms.definition: A companion style with letterforms redrawn on a cursive model, not merely slanted, used for emphasis and titles.

terms.name: Kinetic typography
terms.definition: Type animated over time, where letters and words move, scale, stagger, or morph so the setting carries tone and emphasis a static line cannot.

terms.name: Leading
terms.definition: The vertical distance from one baseline of type to the next, which sets how a paragraph holds together as a block.

terms.name: List virtualization
terms.definition: Rendering only the rows currently in view and a small buffer around them, while spacers preserve the scrollbar of the full list.

terms.name: Marching ants
terms.definition: The animated dashed outline that circles a selection, moving continuously so the boundary reads as active rather than drawn.

terms.name: Meter
terms.definition: A gauge of a known quantity within a known range, such as disk used or password strength, where the level is a fact rather than a task.

terms.name: Model selector
terms.definition: The control in an assistant interface that picks which model answers, usually a menu carrying a short description of each option.

terms.name: Multi-window mode
terms.definition: A windowing mode where two or more apps share one screen, side by side, stacked, or as freeform windows, so every app must survive being any size.

terms.name: Node graph
terms.definition: A canvas of boxes wired to each other by lines, where each box does one job and the wiring between them is the thing being built, rearranged by dragging.

terms.name: Opacity
terms.definition: How much of what is behind an element shows through it, applied to the whole element and its children at once rather than to a single colour value.

terms.name: Overscroll
terms.definition: Scrolling input that continues after a scroller has reached its limit, which platforms answer with a bounce, a glow, or a handoff to the parent.

terms.name: Passkey
terms.definition: Signing in with a device-held credential unlocked by the reader's own biometric or screen lock, so the interface asks for a face or fingerprint, not a secret.

terms.name: Pointer cancellation
terms.definition: Activating a control on pointer release rather than press, so someone who lands on the wrong target can slide off and abort.

terms.name: Pressure sensitivity
terms.definition: Reading how hard a pen or finger presses, plus tilt and twist, so stroke weight and behaviour vary with the shape of the contact.

terms.name: Psychedelic style
terms.definition: A 1960s poster style of vibrating complementary color, warped and interlocking lettering that fills its own shape, kaleidoscopic symmetry, and liquid distortion.

terms.name: Rating
terms.definition: A row of stars or similar marks that both shows a score and, when interactive, takes one.

terms.name: Required field indicator
terms.definition: How a form says a field cannot be left empty, in the label text, in the announced name, and not by an asterisk whose meaning is explained somewhere else.

terms.name: Rotor
terms.definition: VoiceOver's dial for choosing what a swipe or flick moves between: headings, links, landmarks, form controls, or characters.

terms.name: Screen reader
terms.definition: Software that speaks or brailles the accessibility tree and supplies its own keyboard commands for moving through a page.

terms.name: Search field
terms.definition: A text input specialised for queries, with a magnifier, a clear control and often suggestions that appear as you type.

terms.name: Shade
terms.definition: A colour with black mixed in, darker than the original hue and typically used for pressed states, borders and dark theme surfaces.

terms.name: Slide to confirm
terms.definition: A control that commits only once its thumb is dragged the length of its track, so the effort of the gesture is the guard against doing it by accident.

terms.name: Sort indicator
terms.definition: The small arrow in a column header showing that the table is sorted by that column and in which direction.

terms.name: Spring animation
terms.definition: Motion driven by a simulated spring (mass, stiffness, damping) instead of a fixed duration, so the element settles rather than stopping on a schedule.

terms.name: Steps left
terms.definition: Telling the reader where they are in a multi step task and how many steps are still to come, so the end of the task is visible from the start.

terms.name: Supporting pane
terms.definition: A secondary pane holding content that only makes sense next to the main pane, placed beside it on wide windows and below it or behind a control on narrow ones.

terms.name: Tabbable
terms.definition: Reachable by the Tab key, as opposed to merely focusable: an element with tabindex of -1 can take focus from script but never from Tab.

terms.name: The fold
terms.definition: The bottom edge of the first screenful, above which content is seen without any scrolling and below which it must be earned.

terms.name: Toggle group
terms.definition: A set of toggle buttons treated as one control, either single select like radios or multi select like a row of formatting toggles.

terms.name: Trick wording
terms.definition: Phrasing a choice so its plain reading is the opposite of its effect, typically through double negatives or a label that describes the wrong outcome.

terms.name: Unsubscribe link
terms.definition: The way out of a mailing list, which the law and the mail clients now both insist is one click, and whose difficulty is the honest measure of a sender.

terms.name: Virtual keyboard
terms.definition: The on screen keyboard a device raises for a field, whose key set the field itself chooses by declaring what kind of value it wants.

terms.name: Wizard
terms.definition: A flow broken into ordered steps with back and next controls, where each step validates before the next one is allowed.
